examples_10.prompt_excerpt: TASK (first 1,500 chars): # ISSUE DESCRIPTION  [BUG][auto] deadcode-trailing-semicolon-empty-stmt: trailing-semicolon empty statement reported as unreachable warning (code=";", col 0-0) ## Description  The dead-code detector emits a `warning`-severity `unreachable_branch` finding whose `code` field is a bare `;` (an empty statement) whenever a `return`/`raise` statement is written with a trailing semicolon. In Python a trailing `;` is a valid (if unusual) statement separator, so `raise X;` parses as `raise X` followed by an empty statement. That empty statement is technically unreachable, but reporting a no-op as actionable dead code is pure noise — there is nothing for the user to "remove"
